title: GEO Agency, GEO Tool, or In-House? What We Learned While Optimizing Our Brand for AI Search
summary: Compare GEO agency, GEO tool, and in-house AI search optimization through Tsenta’s experience, with reported results, trade-offs, and lessons from XLR8 AI.
body_markdown:
Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the work of improving how AI search names and cites a brand. We’re[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) , a job-application agent. This is our account of evaluating three ways to manage that work: hiring a GEO agency, using a GEO tool, or running an in-house workflow.


[XLR8 AI](https://tryxlr8.ai/) is the GEO solution and service provider we chose to help measure and improve Tsenta’s AI search visibility. We’ll explain the decision framework, the trade-offs, and what we learned from execution. Tsenta is the job-search brand undertaking GEO; XLR8 AI provides the GEO platform and support via GEO strategists.


## Introduction: What Tsenta Learned About Choosing a GEO Approach


At Tsenta, our question was practical: should we hire a GEO agency, use a GEO tool, or run the work in-house?


We are a customer of XLR8 AI, a GEO solution that measures and improves how AI search names and cites a brand. This article describes Tsenta’s own reported experience, rather than independently verified benchmarks.


We evaluated the three routes around four things: strategy, execution capacity, technical access, and measurement. Who decides what to publish? Who actually publishes it and makes the site changes? And what evidence tells us whether the work is helping? Those questions gave us a more useful comparison than a list of content-generation features.


We’ll walk through that decision, our campaign experience, and the practical lessons we took from it. We’ll also explain where XLR8 AI’s combination of software, execution, and ongoing strategic support fit our needs. Measurement gets its own scrutiny: GEO effectiveness varies across domains, so our experience should inform your evaluation, rather than serve as a forecast for your brand.


## What Are a GEO Agency, a GEO Tool, and an In-House AI Search Workflow?


The foundational GEO research found that optimization effectiveness varies across domains. We treat it as an experimental discipline: the query and the evidence matter more than a standard publishing checklist.


For our evaluation at Tsenta, agency, tool, and in-house described operating models. They were starting points for questions about ownership, rather than standardized packages with identical capabilities.


### GEO Agency: Evaluate Strategy and Execution Ownership


An agency model puts external help into the workflow. The useful question is what that help actually covers. Who owns query research, analyzes cited sources, recommends fixes, publishes content, and runs the next experiment?


We would ask for explicit ownership at each step. Technical remediation deserves its own question: does the engagement include implementing changes, or does your team receive recommendations to execute? The agency label alone does not answer that.


### GEO Tool: Evaluate Measurement and Actionability


A tool model gives your team software to use in the workflow. Evaluate the path from measurement to action: what does the data tell you to publish or fix next, and who performs that work?


Separate access to analytics from access to strategic support. Ask whether someone helps interpret citation patterns and prioritize experiments. A dashboard and an execution plan are different deliverables.


### In-House GEO: Evaluate Internal Capacity and Control


An in-house workflow puts ownership with your team. Before choosing it, identify who has the skills and time to research queries, interpret citations, publish content, and make technical changes.


Publishing authority and technical access belong in that assessment. We would name an owner for each task before assuming the team can carry the workflow alongside its existing responsibilities.


### Hybrid GEO: Software, Execution, and Strategic Support


[XLR8 AI](https://tryxlr8.ai/) is a GEO solution that measures and improves how AI search names and cites a brand. Its public offering combines analytics and citation tracking with execution across SEO, GEO, Reddit, third-party citations, and on-page work, plus weekly strategist reviews. That makes it a hybrid example: software, implementation, and ongoing strategic support. Tsenta is an XLR8 AI customer; this article reflects our own experience.


One distinction matters across every model. Being **named** means Tsenta appears in an AI response. Having **owned content cited** means a Tsenta-owned page is referenced as a source. Those answer different questions: did the response mention our brand, and did it use our content? We keep those concepts separate without assuming every provider measures them the same way.


## Why GEO Matters in 2025: What Changed for AI Search Measurement by 2026


For us at Tsenta, choosing a GEO operating model means asking two questions: who will do the content and technical work, and who will check whether it earns citations? The 2025 framing should stay separate from the reporting developments below. Those announcements happened in 2026, and we should judge each approach against the capabilities available at the time.


### GEO Complements Established SEO Foundations


As of September 2026, Google says established SEO practices remain relevant to AI Overviews and AI Mode. It requires no additional technical requirements or special optimizations for inclusion. Supporting pages must be indexed and eligible to appear in Search with a snippet. Even then, inclusion is never guaranteed.


That gives us a practical evaluation criterion: a GEO agency, tool, or in-house workflow should preserve the SEO foundations while measuring AI-search visibility. Content execution and measurement need to sit together. Otherwise, publishing more pages tells us little about whether those pages are being cited.


### AI Search Reporting Available by 2026


Bing introduced AI Performance in Webmaster Tools on February 10, 2026. It covers citations across Microsoft Copilot, Bing AI summaries, and selected partner integrations, with citation counts, cited pages, grounding-query samples, and trends. Those citation counts do not indicate ranking or placement.


On June 16, 2026, Bing announced Intents, Topics, Citation Share, and Compare reporting. Citation Share measures a site's percentage of citations for a grounding query. Bing cautions that this is an observational measure, separate from traffic share or a content-quality score.


Google announced dedicated generative-AI performance reports in Search Console on June 3, 2026, with worldwide availability by August 31, 2026. As of September 2026, the reports include impressions, pages, countries, Search devices, and dates. Saying Google offers no separate AI visibility reporting would therefore be outdated.


For our operating-model decision, official reports and platform-level citation tracking belong alongside strategic review. XLR8 AI's public site describes analytics and citation tracking, weekly reviews with strategists, and execution across SEO, GEO, Reddit, third-party citations, and on-page work. That combination provides a way to connect measurement with the next round of work. Its product description alone does not validate our results, and citation metrics should never be treated as traffic metrics.


## Common AI Search Optimization Challenges and Who Solves Them


For us at Tsenta, evaluating an agency, a tool, or an in-house workflow means assigning responsibility. Who decides what to target? Who ships the work? Who can change the site? Who measures what happened? Generic blog output is an insufficient answer on its own.


### Common Challenges Encountered


**1. Unclear strategy ownership.** Ask who owns query research and citation analysis. An agency should explain who turns those findings into priorities. With a tool, ask which decisions the software supports and which require your judgment. In-house, name the person responsible for choosing queries and reviewing what AI models cite.


**2. Insufficient execution capacity.** Ask who writes, reviews, publishes, and maintains the content. The same question applies to all three routes: where does the work land once a recommendation exists? Google warns that generating many pages without adding user value may violate its scaled-content-abuse policy. Evaluate accuracy, relevance, and usefulness alongside publication volume.


**3. Limited technical access.** Ask whether the people doing the work can change crawling controls, internal links, visible page text, and structured data. Google's AI-feature guidance recommends allowing crawling, making pages discoverable through internal links, keeping important content available as text, and matching structured data to visible content. Confirm who implements those changes, including when a separate website owner must approve them.


**4. Incomplete measurement.** Ask for separate reporting on brand visibility, citations of owned pages, identifiable referrals, and conversion signals. These answer different questions: did we appear, was our content cited, did someone click, and did they take action? OpenAI says ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral URLs, so Google Analytics can track identifiable ChatGPT visits. Referral data alone may still undercount AI-assisted discovery.


### Turning Visibility Data Into Work


We want an explicit handoff from finding to action: a query or citation pattern, an assigned owner, a content or technical task, and a follow-up review. Ask an agency to explain that handoff. Ask a tool provider what your team must execute. Ask your own staff whether they have the time and access to finish it.


XLR8 AI's public service scope combines platform analytics and citation tracking with SEO, GEO, Reddit, third-party citation work, on-page execution, and weekly strategist reviews. That scope connects software, execution, and ongoing strategic support to the responsibilities above. It describes the offering; it does not independently prove results. Our evaluation still needs to establish who owns each task and how progress will be measured.


## What to Look for in a GEO Agency, GEO Tool, or In-House Setup


For us at Tsenta, the useful comparison starts with ownership. Who chooses the queries, publishes the content, fixes technical issues, and decides what changes next? We would evaluate an agency, a tool, and an in-house workflow against the same checklist.


### Must-Have Capabilities for AI Search Optimization


**Query research tied to distinct reader needs.** Ask how each proposed page helps a specific reader and what original value it adds. Google's May 2026 guidance warns against creating separate content for every query variation primarily to manipulate rankings or AI responses. A keyword variation alone is a weak publishing brief.


**Clear strategy and execution ownership.** Establish who turns research into briefs, approves content, publishes pages, and implements fixes. Recommendations need an owner. Ask which work the provider completes and which tasks remain with your team.


**Technical access and checks.** Google's AI-feature guidance recommends allowing crawling, making pages discoverable through internal links, keeping important content available as text, and matching structured data to visible page content. Ask who checks these basics, who has permission to change them, and how fixes are verified.


**Citation analysis that leads to action.** Request a sample report and ask what the team would do next. Does it identify a content gap, a page needing revision, or a source worth investigating? We want a connection between the data and the next task.


**A defined review cadence and internal workload.** Clarify who reviews progress, how often priorities change, and what your team must contribute each week. Even a managed service needs clear approval and access responsibilities.


XLR8 AI publicly documents analytics, citation tracking, execution across SEO, GEO, Reddit, third-party citations and on-page work, plus weekly strategist reviews. That supports describing its offering as software, execution, and strategic support. It leaves campaign-specific model coverage, technical permissions, reporting methodology, and deliverable scope to confirm. We would request those details before treating every checklist item as covered.


### Evidence to Request Before Comparing Results


Before comparing headline visibility figures, request the prompt set, models covered, measurement dates, and the visibility numerator and denominator. Ask exactly what counts as a visible appearance and how many responses were evaluated. Without a defined scope, two percentages may describe different tests.


Request the citation methodology too: what counts as a citation, how repeated citations are handled, and whether reporting separates owned content from third-party mentions. Finally, ask which conversion signals are available and how they connect to the reporting. XLR8 AI's public capability descriptions establish what it offers; they do not independently validate a campaign's results.

## How Tsenta Applied GEO to Its Job-Application Brand


We are an XLR8 AI customer. This is our own campaign experience, with a clear distinction between what public pages corroborate and what we report from the campaign.


### Strategy 1: Choose Reader Needs Relevant to Tsenta’s Product


We focused on resume optimization, application automation, bulk applications,[auto-apply comparisons](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-auto-apply-tools-for-jobs) , and[international students on OPT](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-ai-job-application-tools-international-students-opt) . These topics connect directly to what people use Tsenta for. Our product generates role-specific resumes and cover letters from job descriptions, with changes available for review before submission.


International-student content needed equally careful boundaries. Tsenta can surface known sponsorship signals and use work-authorization information in application answers. We do not guarantee sponsorship. The content needed to reflect that distinction.


### Strategy 2: Evaluate Useful Guides and Comparisons


XLR8 AI tied the campaign’s content to specific, high-intent job-search queries. Guides addressed reader needs, while head-to-head comparison pages addressed questions about choosing between Tsenta and alternatives.


[Our public blog](https://tsenta.com/blog) corroborates the subject areas: bulk applications, auto-apply tools, resume optimization, and international students on OPT. Those pages establish that the content exists. They do not independently establish who wrote it, how many pieces the campaign produced, or which pages caused a visibility change. Attribution to XLR8 AI comes from our campaign account.


### Strategy 3: Address Technical Discoverability


In our campaign account, XLR8 AI worked on titles, descriptions, semantic signals, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, llms.txt, canonicals, and JSON-LD structured data. We treated technical cleanup as part of the same workflow as content production.


The llms.txt work deserves a qualification. Google says sites need no new machine-readable files, AI text files, or special schema.org markup to appear in its AI features. We describe llms.txt as a task completed during the campaign. We cannot isolate it as a proven visibility driver or call it a Google eligibility requirement.


### Strategy 4: Track Brand Visibility and Owned-Content Citations


We used AI visibility as a brand-presence measure in monitored AI answers, and tracked citations of Tsenta’s owned content separately. Our campaign account describes weekly visibility experiments across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Perplexity, tracking share of voice and citations.


There is a measurement boundary here. The supplied account does not include an approved numerator, denominator, prompt set, sampling protocol, or citation-deduplication method. These percentages are our reported campaign measurements, rather than independently verified benchmarks or a standardized score readers can compare across providers.


In the first four-week pilot, we reported visibility increasing from about 2% to 14.1%. That was an early signal within our monitoring. Visibility and citations are separate measures; neither figure establishes traffic, signups, or revenue.


### Strategy 5: Combine Software, Execution, and Weekly Reviews


Our chosen workflow combined software, execution, and recurring strategic support. XLR8 AI handled content and technical work, placed strategic Reddit comments in threads already retrieved by LLMs, and ran weekly visibility experiments.


Its public offering describes SEO, GEO, Reddit, third-party citations, and on-page execution alongside analytics, citation tracking, and weekly strategist reviews. That corroborates the operating model. It does not independently validate our campaign results. For us, the useful combination was a way to measure what happened and a team responsible for deciding what to do next.


### Strategy 6: Interpret Results Alongside Other Marketing Activity


We reported AI visibility growth from 2.1% to a peak of 25.3% by early September 2026, a 12x increase. Citations of Tsenta’s owned content grew from 6 to 117, nearly 20x. These are Tsenta’s reported results, with the measurement limitations described above.


We also reported Google rankings moving from pages 4-6 to pages 1-3 for target keywords. We view that as a byproduct of the same content and technical work, with influencer marketing also contributing. The account does not isolate each contribution. We therefore avoid assigning every change to GEO alone or treating search rankings, AI visibility, and customer acquisition as interchangeable outcomes.


XLR8 AI has also documented this engagement in a case study, “How Tsenta Grew AI Visibility 12x with XLR8 AI.” It covers the starting point (agencies producing generic posts, 2.1% AI visibility, and Google rankings on pages 4 to 6) and the work behind the results: 50+ query-mapped blog posts, 20+[head-to-head comparison pages](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-competitors) , metadata updates across 36+ pages, technical cleanup, Reddit comments, and weekly visibility experiments across 10 categories. The measurement limits above apply to every figure in it.


## Best Practices and Lessons From Comparing GEO Approaches


For us at Tsenta, a useful GEO evaluation needs to separate documented requirements from ideas worth testing. These six lessons provide a practical framework for comparing an agency, a tool, or an in-house workflow without confusing publishing activity with progress.


### Lesson 1: Define the Baseline Before Optimizing


Before comparing results, specify the queries, models, observation dates, and definition of visibility. Record brand mentions and citations separately. Keep the measurement scope consistent, and flag any changes to it.


We would ask the same questions of all three operating models: What are we measuring? Against which baseline? A percentage means little when the query set or measurement method changes halfway through the evaluation.


### Lesson 2: Turn Measurement Into Assigned Actions


Give every recommendation an owner. Someone needs to own publishing, someone needs to own technical fixes, and someone needs to review whether those changes affected the measured results. One person can cover several roles, provided the responsibilities are explicit.


Our evaluation standard is straightforward: a report should lead to a prioritized action, an accountable person, and a review date. Apply that standard whether the work sits with an agency, a tool-assisted team, or an in-house hire.


### Lesson 3: Publish for Distinct Reader Needs


Google warns that producing many AI-generated pages without adding user value may violate its scaled-content-abuse policy. Its guidance emphasizes accuracy, quality, and relevance across content and metadata. Publication volume alone is a poor measure of useful work.


Google’s May 2026 guidance also warns against creating separate pages for every query variation primarily to manipulate rankings or AI responses. For Tsenta’s query-focused content, the editorial test should be a distinct reader need and original value. If two proposed pages answer essentially the same question, reconsider whether both deserve to exist.


### Lesson 4: Check Search Access Without Assuming Special Files Are Required


OpenAI distinguishes OAI-SearchBot, its search crawler, from GPTBot, its training-related crawler. Their robots.txt controls are independent. OpenAI recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot and its published IP ranges to support inclusion in ChatGPT search results. Search access and training access are separate decisions.


Google says its AI features do not require new machine-readable files, AI text files, or special schema.org markup. We would therefore evaluate llms.txt as a campaign task or hypothesis, rather than a Google requirement or a proven visibility lever. A technical checklist should make that distinction explicit.


### Lesson 5: Combine Visibility Data With Referral and Discovery Signals


OpenAI says ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral URLs, making incoming visits identifiable in analytics platforms such as Google Analytics. Saying analytics misses all AI traffic would be too broad. Referral analytics alone may still undercount AI-assisted discovery.


For evaluation, we recommend combining identifiable ChatGPT referrals, platform-specific visibility reporting, and a post-signup “How did you hear about us?” survey. These answer different questions: whether a brand appeared, whether someone clicked, and how someone remembers discovering it. This is a recommended framework, rather than a claim that Tsenta used every attribution method.


### Lesson 6: Treat Format, Reddit, and Model Findings as Observations


Format preferences, Reddit citation patterns, model-specific changes, and publishing-consistency findings should stay tied to the campaign that produced them. Before turning any finding into advice, record the query set, model, observation dates, and supporting examples.


We would treat those findings as hypotheses to test again. A format earning citations in one evaluation does not establish a universal preference. Likewise, a change on one model or after a publishing pause needs its own evidence before it becomes an optimization rule.

Evaluate a tool’s recommendations alongside the people available to execute them. Analytics access does little for a team with no capacity to write, publish, make technical changes, or review the next round of results.

Technical recommendations need someone with permission to implement them. When evaluating any route, we would identify who can change site content, metadata, and technical settings, and who approves those changes.


In-house feasibility therefore depends on more than having a capable writer. An outside provider also needs a workable implementation process. Direct internal control may be preferable when your team already has the necessary access and sustained execution capacity.

Look for a clear review process alongside the dashboard. XLR8 AI describes analytics and citation tracking with weekly strategist reviews. That combination appealed to us because measurement and decisions could sit in the same workflow.

### Internal Workload and Control


Our in-house planning assumption was a tool plus a capable growth hire or intern spending roughly a third of their time on the work. That was our estimate, not a staffing benchmark for every company.


A hybrid model appealed to us because we wanted execution and strategic support together. In-house may suit a team that prefers direct control and can sustain the workload. The useful comparison is who owns each task, what access they have, and whether they can keep doing it.

### How should brands define and measure AI visibility?


Define the queries, models, observation period, and counting rules before interpreting an AI visibility percentage. Keep the signals separate: a brand mention names Tsenta; an owned-content citation references our content; an identifiable referral records a visit; a conversion signal records an action such as signup. Those measures answer different questions. GEO research addresses visibility in generated responses, while referral analytics measures incoming traffic. We would report each signal separately and avoid treating citations as proof of placement or conversions. Any campaign percentage also needs its measurement scope explained alongside it.
